title: Software Engineer
shortDesc: Designs, builds, and maintains software applications and systems.
outlookNote: Employment of software developers is projected to grow much faster than the average for all occupations through 2033, driven by demand for cloud, AI, and cybersecurity software.

title: Web Developer
shortDesc: Builds and maintains websites and web applications.
outlookNote: E-commerce growth and the shift of business tooling to the browser keep web developer demand growing faster than average, though pay varies widely with stack and seniority.

title: Data Scientist
shortDesc: Analyzes large datasets and builds statistical and machine-learning models.
outlookNote: Data scientist roles are among the fastest-growing in the economy as AI adoption spreads from tech firms into healthcare, finance, and retail.

title: Cybersecurity Analyst
shortDesc: Protects computer networks and systems from breaches and attacks.
outlookNote: Ransomware and regulatory pressure have made security one of the tightest hiring markets in tech, with double-digit projected growth through 2033.

title: Network Administrator
shortDesc: Installs, configures, and maintains an organization's networks and servers.
outlookNote: Cloud migration is reshaping rather than shrinking the role — administrators who add cloud and security skills command the strongest offers.

title: IT Support Specialist
shortDesc: Provides technical help and troubleshooting to computer users.
outlookNote: Help desk work remains the most common on-ramp into tech careers, and pay climbs quickly for specialists who move into systems or security roles.

title: Registered Nurse
shortDesc: Provides and coordinates patient care in hospitals, clinics, and other settings.
outlookNote: An aging population and high turnover keep demand for registered nurses strong in every state, with hospitals competing on pay and sign-on bonuses.

title: Nurse Practitioner
shortDesc: Diagnoses conditions, prescribes treatment, and manages patient care independently or with physicians.
outlookNote: Nurse practitioner is one of the fastest-growing occupations in the country as states expand NP practice authority to cover physician shortages.

title: Physician Assistant
shortDesc: Examines, diagnoses, and treats patients under physician supervision.
outlookNote: PAs are increasingly the front line of primary and specialty care, and projected growth remains far above average through 2033.

title: Pharmacist
shortDesc: Dispenses medications and advises patients and clinicians on drug therapy.
outlookNote: Retail pharmacy consolidation has cooled hiring, but clinical and hospital pharmacist roles continue to pay strong six-figure salaries in every state.

title: Physical Therapist
shortDesc: Helps injured or ill people improve movement and manage pain.
outlookNote: Aging baby boomers and sports-medicine demand keep PT employment growing much faster than average, especially in outpatient clinics.

title: Occupational Therapist
shortDesc: Helps patients develop or recover the skills needed for daily living and working.
outlookNote: Demand from schools, home health, and rehabilitation facilities keeps OT hiring steady, with home-health roles typically paying the premium.

title: Dental Hygienist
shortDesc: Cleans teeth, examines patients for oral disease, and provides preventive care.
outlookNote: A persistent post-pandemic hygienist shortage has given the profession unusual wage leverage, with many practices raising hourly rates to fill chairs.

title: Dentist
shortDesc: Diagnoses and treats problems with patients' teeth, gums, and mouth.
outlookNote: Practice ownership versus associateship drives enormous pay spread among dentists; BLS top-codes the highest earners, so real top-decile income runs higher than published figures.

title: Veterinarian
shortDesc: Diagnoses and treats diseases and injuries in animals.
outlookNote: Pet-care spending has proven recession-resistant, and a national shortage of veterinarians keeps signing bonuses and relocation packages common.

title: Medical Assistant
shortDesc: Handles clinical and administrative tasks in physicians' offices and clinics.
outlookNote: Medical assisting is one of the fastest-growing entry points into healthcare, and many employers now fund upskilling into nursing or technologist roles.

title: Licensed Practical Nurse
blsTitle: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
shortDesc: Provides basic nursing care under the direction of RNs and physicians.
outlookNote: Long-term care and home health drive steady LPN demand, and LPN-to-RN bridge programs make this a common stepping-stone credential.

title: Radiologic Technologist
shortDesc: Performs X-rays and other diagnostic imaging examinations.
outlookNote: Imaging volume grows with the aging population, and techs who add CT or MRI certifications typically jump a full pay band.

title: Accountant
shortDesc: Prepares and examines financial records, taxes, and compliance reports.
outlookNote: A shrinking CPA pipeline and steady regulatory complexity keep accountant salaries rising, especially for licensed CPAs.

title: Financial Analyst
shortDesc: Evaluates investments, budgets, and financial performance for businesses.
outlookNote: Analyst pay is heavily concentrated in finance hubs, and bonuses — not captured in base-salary statistics — can add 20–100% in banking roles.

title: Financial Advisor
shortDesc: Advises individuals on investments, retirement, insurance, and estate planning.
outlookNote: Advisor income is unusually spread out because much of it is commission- or AUM-based; the top decile is top-coded in federal data.

title: Marketing Manager
shortDesc: Plans and directs marketing programs, pricing, and brand strategy.
outlookNote: Marketing manager pay is highly concentrated in metros with large corporate headquarters and tech sectors, producing wide state-to-state spreads.

title: Human Resources Manager
shortDesc: Plans and coordinates an organization's recruiting, compensation, and employee relations.
outlookNote: Pay transparency laws and hybrid-work policy demands have raised the strategic profile — and the pay — of senior HR roles.

title: Management Analyst
shortDesc: Advises organizations on improving efficiency, structure, and profits.
outlookNote: Consulting demand tracks corporate restructuring cycles; large-firm consultants in major metros far out-earn the occupation's median.

title: Project Manager
shortDesc: Plans, budgets, and oversees projects across industries.
outlookNote: Project management pay varies sharply by industry — tech and construction PMs typically out-earn the occupation median by 15–30%.

title: Insurance Agent
shortDesc: Sells life, health, property, and casualty insurance policies.
outlookNote: Commission structures mean reported wages understate what established agents with a book of business actually earn.

title: Real Estate Agent
shortDesc: Helps clients buy, sell, and rent residential and commercial property.
outlookNote: Agent income swings with local housing markets and commission splits; high-cost states produce dramatically higher earnings per transaction.

title: Electrician
shortDesc: Installs, maintains, and repairs electrical power, lighting, and control systems.
outlookNote: Grid modernization, EV charging infrastructure, and data-center construction are pushing electrician demand well above historical norms.

title: Plumber
shortDesc: Installs and repairs piping, fixtures, and water and gas systems.
outlookNote: An aging workforce and steady construction demand mean licensed plumbers — especially union journeymen — command strong wages in most states.

title: Carpenter
shortDesc: Constructs and repairs building frameworks and structures.
outlookNote: Housing shortages across most states keep framing and finish carpenters busy, with union commercial work paying the strongest rates.

title: HVAC Technician
blsTitle: Heating, Air Conditioning, and Refrigeration Mechanics and Installers
shortDesc: Installs and services heating, cooling, and refrigeration systems.
outlookNote: Heat-pump adoption and electrification incentives are creating a multi-year boom in HVAC work, and techs with EPA certifications are in short supply.

title: Welder
shortDesc: Joins metal parts using welding equipment in manufacturing and construction.
outlookNote: Certified pipe and structural welders — especially those willing to travel — earn far above the occupation median, with per-diem pay on top.

title: Machinist
shortDesc: Operates machine tools to produce precision metal parts.
outlookNote: Reshoring of manufacturing and CNC automation have raised demand for machinists who can program as well as operate.

title: Auto Mechanic
shortDesc: Inspects, maintains, and repairs cars and light trucks.
outlookNote: EV and advanced driver-assistance systems are splitting the trade: technicians with high-voltage certifications command a growing premium.

title: Construction Manager
shortDesc: Plans, budgets, and supervises construction projects from start to finish.
outlookNote: Infrastructure spending and data-center construction keep experienced superintendents and project executives in exceptionally high demand.

title: High School Teacher
shortDesc: Teaches academic subjects to students in grades 9 through 12.
outlookNote: Teacher pay varies more by state than almost any other profession, because salaries are set by district schedules and state funding formulas.

title: Elementary School Teacher
shortDesc: Teaches basic academic and social skills to students in kindergarten through grade 5.
outlookNote: District salary schedules mean pay rises predictably with years of service and graduate credits — and varies enormously by state funding.

title: Preschool Teacher
shortDesc: Educates and cares for children younger than kindergarten age.
outlookNote: State-funded pre-K expansion is lifting both demand and — in states that fund it — pay, though private childcare wages remain low.

title: College Professor
shortDesc: Teaches courses and conducts research at colleges and universities.
outlookNote: Tenure-track positions pay far above the adjunct-heavy median; field matters enormously, with business, engineering, and health faculty at the top.

title: School Counselor
shortDesc: Helps students develop academic, career, and social skills.
outlookNote: Student mental-health funding has expanded counselor hiring in most states, with pay following district teacher schedules plus a stipend.

title: Police Officer
shortDesc: Enforces laws, responds to emergencies, and patrols assigned areas.
outlookNote: Recruiting shortages have pushed many departments to raise base pay and offer signing bonuses, widening the gap between high- and low-paying states.

title: Firefighter
shortDesc: Responds to fires, medical emergencies, and other hazards.
outlookNote: Base salary understates firefighter earnings — overtime, hazard pay, and pension value add substantially, especially in large city departments.

title: Social Worker
blsTitle: Child, Family, and School Social Workers
shortDesc: Helps children and families cope with challenges and access services.
outlookNote: Government and school-based positions anchor the profession's pay; licensed clinical social workers (LCSW) earn a meaningful premium.

title: Lawyer
shortDesc: Advises and represents clients in legal matters and transactions.
outlookNote: Legal pay is bimodal: large-firm associates start near $200K while public-sector and small-firm lawyers earn a fraction of that — the median hides two distinct markets.

title: Paralegal
shortDesc: Supports lawyers by researching, drafting documents, and organizing cases.
outlookNote: Law firms are pushing more substantive work to paralegals to control billing costs, lifting both demand and the ceiling for senior paralegals.

title: Civil Engineer
shortDesc: Designs and oversees infrastructure: roads, bridges, water systems, and buildings.
outlookNote: Federal infrastructure funding has created a multi-year backlog of public works projects, and PE-licensed engineers are the bottleneck.

title: Mechanical Engineer
shortDesc: Designs, develops, and tests mechanical devices and systems.
outlookNote: Aerospace, EV, and battery manufacturing growth is pulling mechanical engineers into some of the best-funded industrial projects in decades.

title: Truck Driver
shortDesc: Transports goods over intercity and regional routes in heavy trucks.
outlookNote: Freight volumes tied to e-commerce keep long-haul demand steady, while pay depends heavily on route type, endorsements, and whether drivers are paid per mile or per hour.

title: Graphic Designer
shortDesc: Creates visual concepts for brands, products, and publications.
outlookNote: In-house brand and product design roles now out-hire agencies, and designers with UI/UX skills cross into significantly higher tech pay bands.

title: Chef
shortDesc: Directs kitchen operations and prepares meals in restaurants and hotels.
outlookNote: Executive chef and hotel food-and-beverage roles pay far above line-level kitchen wages, and resort markets add housing or seasonal premiums.
